title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

reading.body:
This is a case of an automated alert being treated as a confirmed identification. License plate cameras flagged plates, and deputies acted on that flag by surrounding a car with at least five patrol cars and a helicopter, drawing guns and handcuffing the two men inside. The stop happened at the point where a camera-generated match was converted into an armed detention, before anyone had verified that the car in front of them was the car the system was pointing at.

The verification step was available and was not completed. Deputies could not read the plates on the car they had stopped, which means the match was never confirmed at the scene, and they only recognised the error after the men were handcuffed, when they showed them a photo of the actual stolen vehicle. Catching this would have required reading the plates on the stopped car before the detention escalated, or treating an unconfirmed camera flag as a reason to look rather than a reason to draw weapons.

What is not established is whether the camera misread a plate, whether any deputy violated procedure, and whether the men's account of the threat to shoot will be borne out. The sheriff's office has said supervisors will review body worn camera footage, and no finding has been reported. The men are not facing charges and have said they plan to file complaints.

reports.title: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say

summary:
On Aug. 3 in Cypress, Texas, Harris County sheriff's deputies mistook two 19-year-old men, Anthony and Julian, for car thieves. Deputies surrounded Anthony's Camaro with at least five patrol cars and a helicopter, pointed guns, handcuffed them, and one deputy threatened to shoot, according to the men. The deputies thought the car was a stolen Camaro linked to aggravated robberies after license plate cameras flagged plates, but they could not read the plates on the car they stopped.

After handcuffing the men, deputies realized it was the wrong car and showed them a photo of the stolen vehicle. The men are not facing charges and plan to file formal complaints. Anthony's mother plans to hire an attorney. The sheriff's office says supervisors will review body worn camera footage to check whether procedures and protocols were followed.
title_en: 'I'm going to shoot you': 2 men held at gunpoint before deputies realize their mistake, victims say
